government.note: On 1 January 2000 this tag is the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (FRY), a federation of the Republic of Serbia (including Vojvodina and Kosovo, the latter under UN administration since June 1999) and the Republic of Montenegro. Wikipedia classes it as a federal parliamentary republic (1992-2000) and a federal semi-presidential republic (2000-2003; the federal President was directly elected in September 2000); the effective executive is set to the federal President, the office Slobodan Milošević held in January 2000. On 4 February 2003 the FRY became the State Union of Serbia and Montenegro, with a President who also chaired the Council of Ministers and a unicameral Assembly delegated by the republic parliaments. After Montenegro's independence (3 June 2006) Serbia continued the state's legal personality; under the 2006 Constitution Serbia is a parliamentary republic with a directly elected President (five-year term, two terms at most) and a Government responsible to the 250-member National Assembly. The office records below follow the continuing state: federal offices until 2006, Serbian offices afterwards. The Serbian republic-level President and Prime Minister of 2000-2006 are kept as separate offices (role 'other'). Vojvodina's provincial institutions are not modelled.

name.en: Federal Assembly / National Assembly of Serbia

system.note: 108 members from Serbia and 30 from Montenegro. seats_2000 is the result of the November 1996 federal election; coalitions are recorded under their leading party (the Left Coalition SPS–JUL–ND under SPS, Coalition Together under SPO, the For a Better Life coalition led by DPS in Montenegro under DPS). Others: List for Sandžak (1), Vojvodina Coalition (2) and the Party of Democratic Action of Montenegro (1). The DPS split in 1997 (Momir Bulatović founded the SNP), so the Montenegrin seats had realigned by 2000; this was not checked. The Federal Assembly was replaced by the Assembly of Serbia and Montenegro in 2003.

system.note: In 2000 the assembly of the Republic of Serbia (a constituent republic); the national legislature of the continuing state since June 2006. 250 members elected by list PR. seats_2000 is the result of the September-October 1997 election, with the Left Coalition (SPS–JUL–ND) under SPS; others: Vojvodina Coalition (4), List for Sandžak (3), Democratic Alternative (1) and the Democratic Coalition Preševo-Bujanovac (1).

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Derived from the November 1996 federal Chamber of Citizens vote in both republics (shares computed from the vote counts): SPS–JUL–ND Left Coalition 42.4% plus the Yugoslav Left in Montenegro 0.1% (left populist; SPS's article lists social democracy and populism), Coalition Together 22.2% (classical liberal after its leading party SPO), Serbian Radical Party and splinter lists 19.6% (ethno-nationalist), Vojvodina, Hungarian, Sandžak, Croat and Montenegrin Bosniak minority lists 6.1% (regionalist), DPS-led list 3.4% and SDP 0.6% in Montenegro (social democrat), People's Party (Montenegro) and Serb Union lists 1.8% (national conservative), communist lists 0.8%; remaining lists about 3.1% (big tent). ruling_parties lists the federal government parties (SPS with the Montenegrin SNP; JUL is included under SPS).

claims.note: Kosovo was part of the FRY (under UN administration since June 1999) in 2000. It declared independence on 17 February 2008; the Government of Serbia does not diplomatically recognise Kosovo as a sovereign state (International recognition of Kosovo article).
